minutes.headline: Committee approved carrying over open purchase orders and released class of 2023 funds, and accepted a furniture donation.
minutes.summary: A brief remote School Committee meeting with routine business: minutes, carryover of open purchase orders, the class of 2023 fund release, and a donation of office furniture. Committee reports covered the Finance Committee and future topics including a Turkey Hill forum. The committee then entered executive session on non-union negotiations.

votes.motion: Approve regular session minutes of May 24th and June 7th 2023
Accept the carryover of open purchase orders
Release the class of 2023 funds under the care and custody of the two class officers
Accept the donation of office furniture from the greater Worcester Community Foundation
Enter executive session for non-union negotiations strategy and adjourn at its conclusion
votes.outcome: roll call taken; four yes votes heard

budget_items.what_was_said: The business manager explained that open POs are carried into the next fiscal year awaiting final invoices such as June utility bills. Total was mentioned as around the figure heard.
Purchases were made under a late DESE grant and a Department of Public Health grant for nursing supplies.
A vehicle requisition is on the list though it is town capital money and may fall off the list.
A member asked why an encumbrance exists for the solar energy vendor; the answer was a final invoice is pending for a fee to find buyers.
The class has a remaining balance, verified, requested to be released for future class events.
Report of guard rail repair bids, Page Street culvert, street light bids and abatements funded from ARPA.

decisions.decision: The chair or a member will ask the municipal building committee chair whether to meet over the summer about Turkey Hill's future use.
The chair will circulate dates for an August meeting to review protocols and last year's goals.

what_happened.line: The School Committee voted 4-0 by roll call, as heard, to accept the carryover of open purchase orders into the next fiscal year.
The committee voted 4-0 by roll call, as heard, to release the class of 2023 funds to the two class officers.
The committee voted 4-0 by roll call, as heard, to accept a donation of office furniture from the greater Worcester Community Foundation.
The chair will circulate dates for an August meeting to review protocols and last year's goals.
The committee agreed to ask the municipal building committee chair whether to meet over the summer about Turkey Hill's future use.

why_it_matters: Carried-over purchase orders are bills for this year, such as June utilities, that are paid from the budget after the year closes, so they bear on how much the school budget has left.
The Turkey Hill discussion is an early step on a town building's future use, and it has no decision yet.
